title: 外骨骼救得了耐克吗？
content: Chinese sportswear brands are racing into exoskeleton technology as traditional athletic wear growth stalls. Arc'teryx, Nike, Anta, and Pathfinder have launched powered exoskeleton pants, shoes, and joint supports promising AI-assisted movement. These products generate strong social media buzz and offer brands a fresh "AI narrative" to attract investors. However, consumer-grade exoskeletons face significant hurdles: high prices reaching $1,000+, limited 2-4 hour battery life, and AI algorithms struggling with complex terrain. While the market could grow to $64 billion by 2034, current technology remains immature for mainstream outdoor use, leaving brands seeking compelling reasons for ordinary consumers to purchase.

title: Kimi 叫停新订阅后，如何用上 K3
content: Kimi's K3 model remains accessible via API after new subscriptions were halted, though availability is limited by server capacity and requires paid credits. Testing K3 through four methods—API direct connection, Claude Code integration, Kimi's native client, and OpenAI's Codex—revealed that the same model behaves differently depending on its "harness." Direct API was fastest but offered no process feedback; Claude Code enabled iterative debugging but introduced execution errors and visual style drift; official clients provided the most polished results. The comparison demonstrates that "wrappers" add substantial value through tool orchestration, error handling, and workflow integration, rather than merely repackaging raw model output.

title: AI不到两小时搞定一章博士论文，菲尔兹奖还能撑到2030年吗？
content: Leading AI researchers and mathematicians predict AI will soon surpass human ability in advanced mathematics, potentially making top prizes like the Fields Medal obsolete by 2030. Fields Medalist Timothy Gowers demonstrated ChatGPT 5.5 Pro could produce original, publication-worthy mathematical research in under two hours with zero human input. The model solved problems in additive combinatorics and disproved a long-standing conjecture, with experts confirming the proofs' validity and novelty. This raises fundamental questions about evaluating human contribution, academic credit, and the purpose of mathematical research when AI generates proofs faster than humans can verify them.
